deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface
>
with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in\n> the UI.\n> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API

.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable
or secret manager; never commit it to\n source control or ship it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integ
ration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n

* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in
 [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `
401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the key\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used; crea

te a new key
from [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers
are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept\nan empty `{}`). **Reads**, the catalog listings and eval-run polling, are\n`GET` and tak

e their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource object directly |
| Collection | `{ "items": [...], "nextCursor\
": \"...\" }`; `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error | `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }

` with a matching HTTP status |

**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's
`nextCursor` as `cu

rsor` in the next request (body field on `POST` lists,
query parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque; don't parse them.
**Authoring vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** a
nd responds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything; author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpa
rt: it validates and creates a run synchronously, then\ndetaches execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-run

s/{runId}` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is di
scoverable through the API\nitself: `GET /projects` lists your projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's
servers, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`\nlists its eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key\

nacts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body `{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`
is stable and machine-re

adable; `message` is human-readable and may change;
`details` is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| -
| - | - |\n| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP ser
ver** needs an OAuth grant; distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection
and asked for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine; see [Sign-in challenge
s](#sign-in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid but not allowed to do this, or the **target MCP server** rejected th
e credentials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different MCPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VA
LIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT`
| 409 | The resource isn't in a state that accepts this write, such as a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an enviro
nment that can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support t
his MCP capability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests; see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502
| Could not connect to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |\n

| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

New error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
n

on-retryable failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.

### Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection an

d ask for sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never starts a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 fro
m the MCP server** on `tools/call`: the API answers\n `403 AUTH_REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\
n its `source` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, and\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **A
n `isError` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`** (the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolR
esult` is returned\n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge` field (`source:\n \"tool_result_meta\"`). A field the server alr

eady set under that name is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQUIRED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a differen
t\nkey will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server yourself, upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-account

s), and call again. See
[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Eac
h key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up to **10**.\nExceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-

After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ \

ittered exponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tuned during the preview.

Other `429`s, the per-minute brakes and d
aily budgets described with the\nendpoints below, carry `Retry-After` whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordi
nary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather than a guarantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs\n

your backoff, so **never** block waiting for a header that may not come.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented (req

uest and response schemas, examples,
and an interactive playground) under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog**: discover

the IDs everything else takes:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET /me` | The account behind the key |
| `GET /orga
nizations` | The organizations the caller belongs to, where `organizationId` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and on
ly ever sees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the key can access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{proj
ectId}/servers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's store
d revisions, newest first: captures of its tools and server info, recorded whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /pro
jects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}` | One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it re
ported. Fields listed in `droppedFields` were too large to store, so they are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/
servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What changed since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, remo
ved and changed, and server info changes with both values. A field listed in `droppedFields.from` or `droppedFields.to` was not st
ored on that side, so a change to it is unknown |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with lat
est-run summaries |\n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients` | List clients, or create one from a template or full config |\
n| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}` | Read, edit, or delete a client. The path segment takes a clie
nt **name or ID** |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}/servers` | Replace the client's server attachments (a replacem
ent; omitted servers are detached) |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}/duplicate` | Copy a client's current config i

nto a new client |
| `GET /chat-sessions` | Chat sessions (`?projectId=&status=&limit=&before=`) |
